stories.headline: PM Takaichi meets British rock band Deep Purple in viral diplomatic moment
stories.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, a lifelong hard rock fan and amateur drummer, hosted legendary British band Deep Purple at her Tokyo office. stories.headline: Imperial family visits Fukushima 15 years after nuclear disaster
stories.summary: Emperor Naruhito, Empress Masako, and Princess Aiko made a two-day visit to Fukushima Prefecture to inspect reconstruction efforts 15 years after the Great East Japan Earthquake and nuclear accident. This was the first time since the disaster that the emperor and his family visited the municipalities where the nuclear accident occurred.

stories.headline: Japan downgrades China relationship status in diplomatic bluebook
stories.summary: Japan's 2026 Diplomatic Bluebook downgraded its description of China-Japan relationship from 'one of the most important bilateral relationships' to 'an important neighboring country,' reflecting strained ties following Takaichi's Taiwan remarks. Chinese officials blamed Takaichi's comments as the root cause of tensions.

stories.summary: Analysis shows Prime Minister Takaichi has spoken to the press less frequently than her recent predecessors since taking office in October, while being more active on social media. Data indicates she spoke with waiting press 34 times in her first five months, less than previous PMs.

stories.headline: Takaichi pushes record budget through Diet with shortened deliberations
stories.summary: Prime Minister Takaichi rushed Japan's record 122.31 trillion yen budget for fiscal 2026 through the Diet after unusually brief deliberations of only 115 hours. The budget was enacted despite criticism of shortened debate time and concerns about Takaichi's hard-line stance during deliberations.

stories.summary: A Chinese man was arrested for illegally entering Emperor Naruhito's residence in central Tokyo's Chiyoda district. The incident occurred at the highly secure imperial residence, which serves as both the Emperor's living quarters and a national symbol.

stories.headline: Japan plans MSDF withdrawal from Antarctic mission
stories.summary: Japan plans to withdraw the Maritime Self-Defense Force from operating its Antarctic research vessel in the early 2030s, transferring responsibility for transporting personnel and supplies to a state agency amid growing security demands on the military.

stories.headline: LDP internal divisions over judicial reform legislation
stories.summary: The Liberal Democratic Party delayed submission of a retrial reform bill after internal lawmakers demanded complete ban on prosecutors' appeals. The rare move shows significant divisions within the ruling party over justice system reforms, with many lawmakers opposing the Justice Ministry's position.
